title: OrkStack
description: The whole deployment: runs, Orkers and pools, the cache, schedules, webhooks, HTTP triggers, concurrency limits, the engine and its dependencies, and retention cleanup with the artifact GC.

panels.title: Runs / min
panels.description: Runs that finished, per minute, over the last 5 minutes. A resumed run counts once: its later endings are left out.

panels.title: Failure ratio, 15 m
panels.description: The share of runs that finished in the last 15 minutes and failed. Each ending of a resumed run counts.

panels.title: Open runs
panels.description: Runs open in the deployment now, each counted once.

panels.title: Pollers
panels.description: Orkers that asked a pool for work in the last 90 seconds. A busy, cordoned or stopping Orker asks for none.

panels.title: Orkers
panels.description: Orkers exporting metrics, each counted once. It can lag up to 5 minutes behind one that stopped.

panels.title: Tasks waiting
panels.description: Tasks waiting for an Orker, across the selected pools.

panels.title: Oldest waiting task
panels.description: How long the longest-waiting task of the selected pools has waited.

targets.expr: count((max by (ork_pool) (ork_pool_backlog_tasks{ork_pool=~"$pool"}) > 0) unless on (ork_pool) (max by (ork_pool) (ork_pool_pollers{ork_pool=~"$pool"}) > 0)) or (sum(max by (ork_pool) (ork_pool_backlog_tasks{ork_pool=~"$pool"})) * 0)

panels.title: Pools with work and nobody polling
panels.description: Pools with tasks waiting and no Orker asking for work: add Orkers, or uncordon them.

panels.title: Temporal reachable
panels.description: The share of the engines' and Orkers' requests to Temporal that succeeded over 5 minutes.

panels.title: Object store outage
panels.description: 1 while any Orker has stopped taking work because object storage does not answer.

panels.title: Finished runs not archived
panels.description: Finished runs the archive sweep could not confirm archived. They are lost if object storage stays down until the cluster deletes them.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: OrkStack alerts firing now, by severity. The watchdog, which always fires, is left out.

defaults.noValue: none firing, or no alert rules loaded

panels.title: Telemetry age
panels.description: Seconds since the newest build-info point arrived. Growing means the telemetry pipeline has stopped.

panels.title: Namespaces not exported here
panels.description: Namespaces whose records go to a sink of their own that exports no metrics; their runs are counted only in the deployment-wide figures.

panels.title: Runs by status
panels.description: Runs that finished, per second, by status. Each ending of a resumed run counts.

panels.title: Run duration
panels.description: Run duration from start to finish, at the 50th, 95th and 99th percentiles. A resumed run's later endings are left out.

panels.title: Attempts that failed, by reason
panels.description: Attempts that ended in failure on the Orkers, the ten most frequent reasons, across every namespace.

panels.title: Submissions refused
panels.description: Submissions the admission gate refused, by reason: a hold, a cap on running runs, or a budget.

panels.title: Tasks by status and failure category
panels.description: Tasks that finished, per second, by status and, for a failure, its category.

panels.title: Recent run failures
panels.description: The engine's run_failed lines, newest first. A namespace exported to a sink of its own shows its run id and namespace only.

panels.title: Task log export
panels.description: Whether any Orker exports task logs; when none does, the Run view shows no task logs.

panels.title: Run duration distribution
panels.description: How long runs took, bucket by bucket; an exemplar opens the trace of one run of that length. A resumed run's later endings are left out.

targets.expr: sum by (ork_deployment, ork_failure_reason) (((ork_deployment_orker_tasks_total{ork_failure_reason=~"INPUT_ARTIFACT_CORRUPT|VALUES_CORRUPT|COMMIT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH|COMMIT_UNDECODABLE|COMMIT_STORE_NOT_CONDITIONAL|PANIC"} - last_over_time(ork_deployment_orker_tasks_total{ork_failure_reason=~"INPUT_ARTIFACT_CORRUPT|VALUES_CORRUPT|COMMIT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH|COMMIT_UNDECODABLE|COMMIT_STORE_NOT_CONDITIONAL|PANIC"}[1d] offset $__rate_interval)) > 0) or ((ork_deployment_orker_tasks_total{ork_failure_reason=~"INPUT_ARTIFACT_CORRUPT|VALUES_CORRUPT|COMMIT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH|COMMIT_UNDECODABLE|COMMIT_STORE_NOT_CONDITIONAL|PANIC"} unless last_over_time(ork_deployment_orker_tasks_total{ork_failure_reason=~"INPUT_ARTIFACT_CORRUPT|VALUES_CORRUPT|COMMIT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH|COMMIT_UNDECODABLE|COMMIT_STORE_NOT_CONDITIONAL|PANIC"}[1d] offset $__rate_interval)) and on (ork_deployment) (count by (ork_deployment) (last_over_time(ork_build_info[1d] offset $__rate_interval)) > 0))) > 0 or vector(0)

panels.title: Integrity failures
panels.description: Attempts that found stored data not what was written, by reason, across every namespace, the first of a reason included. Never a workload's fault: shown even at zero.

panels.title: Attempts a task took, p95
panels.description: The attempt number tasks finished on, at the 95th percentile, by pool.

targets.expr: topk(10, max by (ork_namespace, ork_task_id) (max_over_time({service_name=~".*orker"} | ork_record="usage" | ork_usage_kind="summary" | ork_namespace=~"$namespace" | unwrap ork_attempt [$__interval])))

panels.title: Most-retried tasks
panels.description: The ten tasks whose attempts reached the highest attempt number, from the Orkers' usage summaries.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (ork_namespace, ork_task_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~".*orker"} | ork_record="usage" | ork_usage_kind="summary" | ork_namespace=~"$namespace" | unwrap ork_usage_cpu_seconds [$__interval])))

panels.title: Tasks that used the most CPU
panels.description: The ten tasks whose attempts used the most CPU seconds, from the Orkers' usage summaries.

panels.title: Are there enough Orkers for the work?
Tasks waiting, pollers and Orkers, by pool
panels.description: Per pool: tasks waiting, Orkers asking for work, and Orkers exporting metrics.

panels.title: Oldest waiting task, by pool
panels.description: How long each pool's longest-waiting task has waited. One that never clears while Orkers poll may belong to a release whose Orkers were stopped.

panels.title: Tasks waiting, by release
panels.description: With versioning on, each pool's waiting tasks by the release they wait for; unversioned is what the total holds beyond them, so together they come to the pool's total, approximately. Tasks of a release that never clear while the pool polls belong to a release whose Orkers stopped: a stranded release, not demand.

panels.title: Oldest waiting task, by release
panels.description: With versioning on, how long each release's longest-waiting task of each pool has waited; unversioned tasks have no age of their own. One that grows while the others clear is a stranded release.

panels.title: Tasks arriving and handed out, by pool
panels.description: The cluster's own recent rates for each pool.

panels.title: Running against slots, by pool
panels.description: Tasks running now beside how many the pool's Orkers run at once.

panels.title: Cordoned Orkers, by cause
panels.description: Orkers that take no new work, by why: an operator, an object-store outage, or stopping.

panels.title: Wait before an Orker begins a task, p95
panels.description: Seconds from the cluster scheduling a task's first attempt to an Orker beginning it, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: CPU reserved, share of capacity
panels.description: Per Orker that declares a capacity, the share of the cpu it admits tasks within that stands reserved; the 20 most reserved.

panels.title: Open pins, by pool
panels.description: Pins held open now: groups of tasks sharing one Orker.

panels.title: Live CPU of running tasks
panels.description: The CPU cores running attempts' containers use now: across every Orker, and on the busiest one.

panels.title: Live memory of running tasks
panels.description: The memory running attempts' containers use now, across every Orker and on the largest one, and how many containers were measured.

panels.title: Memory reserved, share of capacity
panels.description: Per Orker that declares a capacity, the share of the memory it admits tasks within that stands reserved; the 20 most reserved.

targets.expr: bottomk(10, max by (ork_namespace, ork_task_id) (max_over_time({service_name=~".*orker"} | ork_record="usage" | ork_usage_kind="summary" | ork_namespace=~"$namespace" | ork_usage_memory_peak_exact="true" | unwrap ork_usage_memory_peak_bytes [$__interval])) / max by (ork_namespace, ork_task_id) (max_over_time({service_name=~".*orker"} | ork_record="usage" | ork_usage_kind="summary" | ork_namespace=~"$namespace" | unwrap ork_reserved_memory_bytes [$__interval])))

panels.title: Most over-reserved tasks
panels.description: The ten tasks whose attempts' peak memory was the smallest share of what they reserved: lower their request.

targets.expr: clamp_min(count by (ork_pool) (ork_orker_present{ork_pool=~"$pool"}) - (max by (ork_pool) (ork_pool_pollers{ork_pool=~"$pool"}) or count by (ork_pool) (ork_orker_present{ork_pool=~"$pool"}) * 0), 0)

panels.title: Why nobody polls
panels.description: Per pool: Orkers exporting metrics that are not asking for work, beside those cordoned. A busy Orker asks for none either: see slots in use.

panels.title: Slots in use, by pool
panels.description: The share of each pool's slots its running tasks fill; at 1 its Orkers ask for no new work.

targets.expr: count(count by (ork_pool) (ork_orker_present{ork_pool=~"$pool"}) unless on (ork_pool) max by (ork_pool) (ork_pool_backlog_tasks)) or vector(0)

panels.title: Pools whose backlog is not measured
panels.description: Pools with Orkers but no backlog reading: name them in engine.pool_metrics.pools.

panels.title: Admission wait, p95
panels.description: How long an Orker's poll waited for room before it was granted, at the 95th percentile, by what bound it, and attempts refused for a request no Orker admits.

panels.title: Attempt phases, p95
panels.description: How long each phase of an attempt took on the Orkers, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Task log export
panels.description: Task log records the Orkers exported, by outcome, and export batches by outcome.

panels.title: Attempt records
panels.description: Attempt records the Orkers wrote, by outcome; one not written leaves an attempt without its record.

panels.title: Left behind or unmeasured
panels.description: Attempts whose workspace could not be removed, whose container's end could not be watched, whose usage could not be measured or sampled, and those stopped at their memory limit.

panels.title: Object store outages
panels.description: Orkers entering and leaving their store-outage cordon.

panels.title: Builds running
panels.description: Each build of ork and orker exporting metrics now, and how many processes run it.

panels.title: Memo hit ratio, by namespace
panels.description: Of cached tasks' memo lookups that were not bypassed, the share that hit.

panels.title: Lookups by outcome and miss reason
panels.description: Cached tasks' memo lookups, by outcome and, for a miss, why.

panels.title: Memo step duration, p95
panels.description: How long the memo step took, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Memo writes by outcome
panels.description: Memo writes after a miss; a failed one costs only the next run's hit.

panels.title: Cached tasks by Orkflow and outcome
panels.description: Tasks of cached steps that finished, per second, by Orkflow and memo outcome.

panels.title: Results reused
panels.description: Memo hits that reused a result and started no container, per second, by pool.

panels.title: Memo step duration against its timeout
panels.description: The memo step's 95th percentile beside its 30-second timeout, after which it is a miss.

panels.title: Fires by outcome
panels.description: Schedule fires the engines prepared, by outcome and, for a refused one, why. An unavailable fire is tried again.

panels.title: Busiest schedules
panels.description: The ten schedules that fired most over the panel's interval. A schedule is named only while telemetry.object_labels is on.

panels.title: Fire lag, p95
panels.description: How long after its nominal time a fire was prepared, at the 95th percentile. A backfill is as late as the time it stands in for.

panels.title: Actions the cluster skipped
panels.description: Schedule actions the cluster did not take, by why: an overlap policy, a missed catch-up window, or a full buffer.

panels.title: Requests by action
panels.description: Schedule requests that succeeded, by action: what people changed, and fires and backfills asked by hand.

panels.title: Schedules by state
panels.description: Schedules active and paused.

targets.expr: count(max by (ork_namespace, ork_schedule) (ork_schedule_next_fire_seconds{ork_namespace=~"$namespace"}) < time() - 600) or vector(0)

panels.title: Overdue schedules
panels.description: Namespaces whose soonest next fire is more than 10 minutes in the past: the cluster is not firing their schedules. With telemetry.object_labels on, each schedule counts.

panels.title: The 20 soonest fires
panels.description: Seconds until the soonest next fire of each namespace, or of each schedule while telemetry.object_labels is on, soonest first.

panels.title: Schedule census
panels.description: The share of schedules the last census read, and 1 while the census cannot read them; then the schedule gauges are stale.

panels.title: Deliveries by outcome
panels.description: Webhook deliveries that settled: delivered, or failed for good after their last attempt.

panels.title: Busiest webhooks
panels.description: The ten webhooks with the most deliveries over the panel's interval. A webhook is named only while telemetry.object_labels is on.

panels.title: Attempts by answer
panels.description: Delivery attempts by what answered: the receiver's status class, a transport error, a request never sent, or one refused.

panels.title: Attempts by number
panels.description: Attempts by their place in the delivery's retry ladder.

panels.title: Attempts per delivery, p95
panels.description: How many attempts a settled delivery took, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Delivery latency, p95
panels.description: How long after it was queued a delivery settled, at the 95th percentile, by outcome.

panels.title: Request duration, p95
panels.description: How long one attempt's request took, at the 95th percentile, by answer.

panels.title: Deliveries pending, by age
panels.description: Deliveries queued and not yet settled, counted by whether they are older than each age.

panels.title: Deliveries not queued
panels.description: Deliveries that could not be queued and so made no request, by why.

panels.title: Recent delivery failures
panels.description: The engine's lines for deliveries that failed for good, newest first. Never the URL.

panels.title: HTTP trigger invocations by outcome
panels.description: Invocations of HTTP triggers, per second, by namespace and outcome. One that named no trigger carries no namespace.

targets.expr: sum by (ork_deployment) (((ork_trigger_invocations_total{ork_namespace=~"$namespace",outcome!="started"} - last_over_time(ork_trigger_invocations_total{ork_namespace=~"$namespace",outcome!="started"}[1d] offset 1h)) > 0) or ((ork_trigger_invocations_total{ork_namespace=~"$namespace",outcome!="started"} unless last_over_time(ork_trigger_invocations_total{ork_namespace=~"$namespace",outcome!="started"}[1d] offset 1h)) and on (ork_deployment) (count by (ork_deployment) (last_over_time(ork_build_info[1d] offset 1h)) > 0))) > 0 or vector(0)

panels.title: Invocations that started no run, 1 h
panels.description: HTTP trigger invocations in the last hour that started no run, whatever the reason.

panels.title: Are concurrency limits holding work back?
Slots held against the limit
panels.description: Per limit and level, the slots held now beside the slots its active keys admit.

panels.title: Keys active and full
panels.description: Per limit, keys holding or queueing anything, and those with every slot held.

panels.title: Queued
panels.description: Runs and tasks waiting for a slot, per limit and level, and runs queued per namespace.

panels.title: Requests for a slot by outcome
panels.description: Requests for a slot, per second, by strategy and how each was answered: granted, queued, refused or skipped, or a limit that could not answer.

panels.title: Waits ended by outcome
panels.description: Waits in line that ended, per second, by how: started, canceled, timed out, superseded, or a limit that could not answer.

panels.title: Wait in line, p95
panels.description: How long a wait in line lasted before it ended, at the 95th percentile, per limit and level.

panels.title: Oldest queued
panels.description: How long the oldest queued entry has waited, per limit and level.

panels.title: Oldest queued, share of its bound
panels.description: The oldest queued entry's wait as a share of how long it may wait; at 1 it is refused.

panels.title: Holders and gates in trouble
panels.description: Holders whose runs keep failing their workflow tasks, gates checking new holders after dropping a fence, and gates rebuilding their record.

panels.title: Slots taken back
panels.description: Slots and places in line a limit took back, per second, because their run no longer holds or waits for them, by why, and the checks of a run that failed, whose slot or place is kept.

panels.title: Limit starts
panels.description: Keys that became active, per second, and the rebuilds of their record: skipped after a clean end, done, or an attempt that failed and is tried again.

panels.title: Concurrency census
panels.description: Gates the last census read and those that did not answer; 1 while it stopped at its gate ceiling, could not run, or a namespace's gate did not answer.

panels.title: Concurrency census age
panels.description: How long the last census pass took, and how old each engine's snapshot is beside the census interval.

panels.title: Concurrency index
panels.description: 1 when the cluster does not index concurrency limits, so the census and submit's checks cannot count them.

panels.title: Is the engine, Temporal and object storage healthy?
API requests by code
panels.description: Requests to the engine's API, per second, by result code.

panels.title: API latency
panels.description: API request duration at the 95th and 99th percentiles.

panels.title: Live streams
panels.description: Run event streams the engines hold open, by kind.

panels.title: Requests to Temporal
panels.description: Requests the engines and Orkers made to Temporal, and those that failed.

panels.title: Long runs carrying on
panels.description: Runs carried forward into a fresh history, by outcome.

panels.title: Saved state written, p95
panels.description: The size of what a run's carrying-on wrote, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Object store requests by operation
panels.description: Requests the engines and Orkers made to object storage, by operation and outcome.

panels.title: Object store latency, p95
panels.description: Object store request duration at the 95th percentile, by operation.

panels.title: Store clock skew
panels.description: The engines' clocks against the object store's: the largest and smallest offset any engine reports.

panels.title: Audit records
panels.description: Control-plane writes recorded, and those the audit store could not take.

panels.title: Telemetry that could not be sent
panels.description: Export errors, and records dropped because their namespace's sink is unknown.

panels.title: Census passes skipped
panels.description: Periodic reads that feed gauges and were skipped by their budget; a gauge whose census is skipped is stale.

panels.title: Carrying on: write, restore and hold, p95
panels.description: How long a switch's write and a whole restore took, and how long runs held new tasks first, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Saved-state reads, p95
panels.description: The attempt each successful read of a saved state succeeded on, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Temporal long polls
panels.description: The engines' and Orkers' long polls to Temporal, and those that failed.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines of the largest process of each service.

panels.title: Go memory in use
panels.description: Memory the Go runtime holds in the largest process of each service.

panels.title: Processes seen
panels.description: Processes of each service exporting metrics now, beside how many the last hour saw: more in the hour means restarts.

panels.title: Collector intake
panels.description: Points, records and spans the Collector accepted, refused and failed, per second.

panels.title: Collector exports waiting
panels.description: Items the Collector holds to send, against how many it can hold.

panels.title: Alert pipeline
panels.description: 1 while the watchdog alert, which always fires, reaches Prometheus: the rules are loaded and evaluating.

panels.title: Are retention cleanup and the artifact GC reclaiming space?
Retention cleanup
panels.description: Whether retention cleanup retires runs past their namespace's retention.

panels.title: Cleanup interval and buffer
panels.description: The cleanup interval, and how far past the maximum run retention the cluster's own backstop sits.

panels.title: Runs cleanup decided on
panels.description: Runs a cleanup pass decided on, by outcome, in the selected namespaces and in all of them.

panels.title: Objects removed by cleanup
panels.description: Run-scoped objects retirement removed.

panels.title: Cleanup passes
panels.description: Cleanup passes by outcome.

panels.title: Cleanup pass duration, p95
panels.description: How long a cleanup pass took, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Cleanup behind retention
panels.description: How far past its due time the most overdue run cleanup left unretired is, and how long since the last complete walk.

panels.title: Cleanup errors by step
panels.description: Cleanup failures by the step that failed; a later pass tries again.

panels.title: Never completed
panels.description: 1 for each walk that has not finished once since its engine started: the archive sweep's full pass, cleanup's complete walk, and a GC pass. Alerts fire on the same.

panels.title: Archive sweep
panels.description: Finished runs the sweep could not confirm archived; 1 while it could not read the run index to its end, or while two intervals reach the cluster's retention.

panels.title: Archive sweep timing
panels.description: Seconds since the last pass that saw everything, and, while runs are unconfirmed, until the first of them expires.

panels.title: Runs the archive sweep came to
panels.description: Finished runs with no archive, by what the sweep did: archived, failed (tried again), or expired (lost).

panels.title: GC mode
panels.description: What the artifact GC does: off, dry_run (reports what it would delete) or delete.

panels.title: GC held
panels.description: 1 while the GC deletes nothing for a reason it reports.

panels.title: Reclaimed
panels.description: Bytes the GC deleted across every namespace, by kind of object.

panels.title: Would delete (dry run)
panels.description: What the last complete dry-run cycle would have deleted.

panels.title: Low-water age
panels.description: The age of the oldest open or unarchived run, which holds back reclamation of everything retired after it.

panels.title: Bytes written by OrkStack against reclaimed
panels.description: Store bytes OrkStack's own flows wrote, beside what the GC reclaimed. Never the bucket's total.

panels.title: GC grace
panels.description: How long a retired run's objects stay before the GC may reclaim them.

panels.title: Bucket keeps versions
panels.description: 1 when the bucket keeps versions, so a GC delete only adds a delete marker and frees nothing.

panels.title: Why the GC is held
panels.description: 1 for each reason the last pass deleted nothing.

panels.title: Objects by outcome
panels.description: Objects the GC dealt with in delete mode, by outcome and why, in the selected namespaces and in all of them.

panels.title: Reclaimed by namespace
panels.description: Bytes the GC deleted, by namespace.

panels.title: Would delete and kept (dry run)
panels.description: The last complete dry-run cycle: objects it would delete, and objects it would keep, by why.

panels.title: Would delete in all namespaces (dry run)
panels.description: The last complete dry-run cycle's bytes across every namespace.

panels.title: GC passes
panels.description: GC passes by outcome.

panels.title: GC pass duration, p95
panels.description: How long a GC pass took, at the 95th percentile.

panels.title: Retired runs the GC came to
panels.description: Retired runs by outcome: finished, carried over, waiting on another run or the low-water mark, or held for good.

panels.title: Runs due and waiting
panels.description: Retired runs the last pass carried over, and those waiting on another run or the low-water mark.

panels.title: Since the GC last moved
panels.description: Seconds since the last pass, and since the last one that finished a run or deleted an object.

panels.title: Low-water mark
panels.description: 1 for the reason the last pass could not compute its low-water mark, and how many open runs its walk read.

list.name: ui_url
list.description: The OrkStack UI's address, for links to a run's page.
